extraction_scope: Worker-6 replaced generic keyword placeholders with source-reviewed mechanism claims from XML/PDF/OA figures; figure-only exact values were not fabricated.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Digitiferin has direct bacterial-surface damage evidence in B. subtilis: SEM after 5 uM treatment showed surface dimpling, roughness, and vesicle coverage, while the structural model presents separated neutral and positive electrostatic regions consistent with membrane interaction.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: digitiferin; B. subtilis mechanism assay context

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=8:Predicted mechanism of action with a digitiferin structural model and observations of digitiferin-treated bacteria using SEM

mechanism_claims.limitations: The model is predictive and SEM is morphological; the final claim is limited to membrane/surface damage evidence, not a single molecular target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Digitiferin induces bacterial aggregation under Table 1 assay conditions; E. coli aggregates at 10 uM include dead cells by trypan-blue staining, supporting aggregation-associated antimicrobial stress without treating MAC as MIC.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: digitiferin; E. coli, S. aureus, and B. subtilis aggregation endpoints
mechanism_claims.limitations: MAC is preserved as an aggregation endpoint and is not promoted to a growth-inhibition MIC endpoint.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Digitiferin is source-localized to coral mucus/epithelial secretion context and has condition-dependent Vibrio killing under low-salt conditions, supporting a first-line mucus-defense model with explicit salt-dependence.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: digitiferin in Acropora digitifera mucus; Vibrio coral pathogens

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=10:Digitiferin expressed in vivo and secreted into coral mucus
xml:sec=11:Digitiferin antimicrobial activity against coral pathogens

mechanism_claims.limitations: The disease-resistance role remains inferential at organism level; the paper itself states direct infection-comparison evidence is still needed.

caution_findings.finding: The paper supports salt-dependent Vibrio killing and mucus localization, but not a direct infection-survival test proving digitiferin determines coral disease resistance.
